sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

content.text:
Case F46: segment the fibrous soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 251x251x498 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case F46 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(251, 251, 498) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: fibrous soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 249/498 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm wondering if this is the knee region, so I should look at the axial slice to confirm.

content.text: sheet axial 20–480/498 (16 slices) | v0 | tool calls 2/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm tracing the lesion from the thigh down through the knee into the lower leg, noting it sits in the popliteal fossa with a heterogeneous bright signal mixed with dark fibrous-looking components—possibly consistent with a desmoid-type tumor. I want to check the sagittal images to confirm this.

content.text: sheet sagittal 70–180/251 (12 slices) | v0 | tool calls 3/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking:
I'm examining the sagittal views of this long volume, trying to locate the lesion near the popliteal region—there's an ovoid moderately bright area that could be in the thigh given the scaled proportions of the 498mm volume.

I'm also cross-referencing the axial slices, noting a posterior moderately bright region in the calf around 265-296 and a differently-signaled posterior area at 235 bounded by a curved line, trying to figure out if this represents the mass. I'm working through the orientation logic (top=superior vs. ankle, how k increases through the volume) to reconcile where the sagittal ovoid region actually sits relative to the axial calf findings.

The heterogeneous bright/dark region with flow voids at the knee level (axial 112-204) could represent a vascular malformation or be the tumor itself, possibly a desmoid-type fibrous tumor with its characteristic dark bands. The more homogeneous, slightly brighter posterior region at axial 265 also fits with intermediate T2 signal typical of fibrous tumors. I should check the coronal images next to clarify.

content.text: sheet coronal 90–200/251 (12 slices) | v0 | tool calls 4/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm trying to orient myself with these coronal and axial views, figuring out where the knee and calf mass sit relative to the volume's superior-inferior axis, since the slice positioning seems inconsistent across views.

content.text: axial 265/498 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 5/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking:
I'm weighing whether the posterior brightness is just muscle edema versus something more significant, and reconsidering the knee lesion - the dark fibrous bands make a fibrous tumor like desmoid plausible, though a vascular malformation can't be ruled out either. I'm also noting that larger ovoid mass-like region above the knee on the coronal images.

I'm trying to sort out orientation - which end of the coronal stack is superior versus inferior, using the artifact line positions and bone counts on various axial slices to figure out whether higher slice numbers correspond to the thigh or the foot. The bone shapes and muscle bulk patterns on each slice aren't lining up cleanly with my assumption, so I'm reconsidering whether slice 20 is really the thigh level or something else entirely.

Actually, I think this is more likely the arm rather than the leg — slice 20 as upper arm near the humerus, moving through the elbow around 150-200, into the forearm with radius and ulna from 235-450, and the wrist near 480. That makes the forearm mass more anatomically sensible regardless of exact orientation. The ovoid structure I noticed near the top of the coronal image at 90-100 lines up with that forearm region around 265, matching the brighter posterior area I'd flagged earlier, and looks like the likely tumor given its homogeneous intermediate-to-high T2 signal and displacement effect, while the mixed bright/dark area near the elbow is probably just normal joint tissue with vessels and fat. I'm settling on the posterior forearm mass as the target, centered around coordinates 1710/1783/1746.

content.text: version v1 (parent v0) | volume 566.6 mL | components 121 (largest 98.5%; 120 others total 8.7 mL) | extent axial 185–462, coronal 56–182, sagittal 95–181 | change +566.6 mL / 0.0 mL | tool calls 6/40, prompts 1/15 | point add (2 mark(s)) | image: axial 323, coronal 98, sagittal 141 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: I'm noting this is a huge 566 mL mass with leakage - the sagittal view shows a well-defined ovoid posterior mass spanning a large portion of the image, and the axial slices show it extending with anterior leak. I want to cross-check the axial mask outline at 265 against the actual mass boundaries to confirm the extent.

content.text: sagittal 141/251 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
This sagittal view looks like a leg with the knee at the bottom and thigh above, though the image seems cropped and it's hard to make out a distinct mass—there's a vague posterior ovoid region worth noting.

Reconsidering the data, I'm now leaning toward the heterogeneous region in the popliteal fossa (axial ~112-204, coronal 130-150) being the tumor—lobulated with mixed dark and bright signal suggesting something like a fibrous tumor or vascular malformation, roughly 120mm in size, while the calf appears more homogeneously bright, possibly just edema or denervation. I want to pull up axial slice 143 with markers to examine the knee lesion more closely.

content.text: axial 150/498 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay none | v1 | tool calls 8/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
I'm looking at the single bone near the heterogeneous mass medial to it — the dark area with a bright rim suggests a fibrous tumor like a desmoid, which often shows low T2 signal with bright components, making this look like a genuine mass rather than a normal structure.

I'll go with the heterogeneous mass spanning those slices as the clear abnormality, undo the earlier box, and place a lasso around the dark region while marking positive points on the dark and bright portions.

I should fill holes and check the extent, which spans axial slices 55-203 for a volume of 314 mL, then view it again after filling.

content.thinking: I'm noticing the mask at slices 166-195 excludes some dark regions that could be bone or muscle near the joint, while bright lobules lateral to the mask at slice 166 look like they might also represent lesion tissue not currently captured.

content.thinking: Looking at axial slice 139, the removed region seems to be a rim of intermediate tissue around a muscle, not the true lesion, while the new mask correctly isolates the dark-and-bright heterogeneous core that represents the actual lesion, including an adjacent vessel. This makes me lean toward v4 as the better segmentation.

content.thinking: I'm noticing some inconsistencies in the mask boundaries — at slice 179 a dark region that was included in a prior version is now excluded, possibly fibrous tumor tissue, and at slice 195 a bright medial-anterior area isn't captured, which could be additional lesion extension or edema/effusion rather than tumor proper.

content.text: axial 182/498 | crop mask | marks coarse | overlay outline | v4 | tool calls 16/40, prompts 3/15

content.thinking: The dark patch between those coordinates looks like it's part of the fibrous lesion, and there's a bright area along the right edge too. I'll mark the dark region as positive points to include it.

content.text:
Final review of v5: volume 325.5 mL | components 4 (largest 99.9%; 3 others total 0.0 mL) | extent axial 38–209, coronal 86–165, sagittal 90–180 | tool calls 18/40, prompts 4/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).
C1 add 725 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
C2 add 590 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
C3 add 419 mL, touches mask on its left, right and posterior sides, mostly inferior of the mask
candidate image: one row per candidate, columns axial / coronal / sagittal through the candidate (green outline = current mask, magenta outline + light tint = candidate; judge the tissue inside the magenta outline). For each candidate decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept) or normal tissue (reject). Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "8293" to save it.

content.thinking: These candidates look like shells, so I'll reject them. Checking the axial slice at 217 past the mask, I notice some mild bright signal at the medial anterior aspect — I'll accept the current finding.

arguments.reason: Heterogeneous mass around joint captured in 3 planes; boundaries with adjacent edema/vessels uncertain.

content.text: case F46 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v5 | final volume 325.5 mL, components 4 (largest 99.9%; 3 others total 0.0 mL) | tool calls 19/40, prompts 4/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

I've saved the final mask for case F46 at medium confidence: 325.5 mL, covering axial slices 38–209.

**What I segmented:** a lobulated mass next to the joint, mixing bright T2 nodules with dark, fibrous-looking areas. It sits next to the single long bone and spans roughly 170 mm along the limb. In the final review the outline followed this mass in all three planes. The mask has 4 pieces, but the main one holds 99.9% of the volume and the rest are tiny fragments.

**Main uncertainty, which structure is the tumor:** further down the limb, past the joint where there are two bones, there is a smooth, slightly bright oval area in the posterior muscles. My first prompt went there and spilled into 566 mL of surrounding tissue, so I dropped that version. I judged that area to be muscle signal change rather than tumor, because the mixed bright/dark mass is the clearly abnormal one. I couldn't confirm that from the images. If the target was actually that posterior region, this mask is on the wrong structure.

**How the mask developed:**
- **Removed:** after I added the bright tissue in front of and beside the mass, the model dropped a band of intermediate-grey tissue around a muscle on the inner side. I accepted that removal, since that band looked like normal muscle.
- **Added:** I then added the dark areas between the bright nodules near the joint, since dark fibrous tissue is typical for this kind of tumor.
- **Rejected:** the three automatic suggestions in the final review were thick rings of normal tissue around the mask.

**Edges that may be off:**
- Just past the joint end of the mask (axial 217) there is a little faint bright tissue on the inner front side that I left out.
- The boundary between the mass and nearby bright vessels or swelling was hard to call in places.

I used 19 of 40 tool calls and 4 of 15 model prompts.
